$schema.description: The JSON Schema this file follows, for editor completion and these descriptions.

name.description: The product's name, shown on the end card.

locale.description: BCP 47 locale (en-US): the recording browser's locale, <html lang> and the language of the copy. Its language needs a message dictionary: en, pl.

timezone.description: IANA zone of the recording browser, e.g. Europe/London.

logo.description: The end card's logo next to the name; without it, the name alone.

svg.description: The logo as an .svg file, relative to the folder of marketing.json.

colors.description: The colour roles as hex colours; a colour set here wins over tokensFrom.

background.description: The frame behind the phone and the vignette; #rrggbb, because the vignette appends an alpha. A hex colour; without it, the colour comes from tokensFrom.

foreground.description: Text on the background: the persona card's name, the end card. A hex colour; without it, the colour comes from tokensFrom.

muted.description: Secondary text: the persona card's tagline, the end card's note. A hex colour; without it, the colour comes from tokensFrom.

accent.description: The touch ring and the end of the avatar's gradient. A hex colour; without it, the colour comes from tokensFrom.

cta.description: The end card's link pill and the start of the avatar's gradient. A hex colour; without it, the colour comes from tokensFrom.

onCta.description: Text on the cta colour. A hex colour; without it, the colour comes from tokensFrom.

captionBackground.description: The caption pill. A hex colour; without it, the colour comes from tokensFrom.

captionText.description: Caption words not spoken yet. A hex colour; without it, the colour comes from tokensFrom.

captionHighlight.description: The word being spoken. A hex colour; without it, the colour comes from tokensFrom.

tokensFrom.description: Where the colours not set in colors come from: the app's stylesheet or an Impeccable design.json.

css.description: The app's stylesheet whose custom properties hold the tokens; give this or designJson.

designJson.description: An Impeccable design.json (schemaVersion 2) holding the tokens; give this or css.

theme.description: Which theme's token values to read.

roles.description: The source token each role reads; by default the role's own name in kebab case (onCta reads on-cta).

background.description: The source token for the background role (The frame behind the phone and the vignette; #rrggbb, because the vignette appends an alpha.) Default: the role's name in kebab case.

foreground.description: The source token for the foreground role (Text on the background: the persona card's name, the end card.) Default: the role's name in kebab case.

muted.description: The source token for the muted role (Secondary text: the persona card's tagline, the end card's note.) Default: the role's name in kebab case.

accent.description: The source token for the accent role (The touch ring and the end of the avatar's gradient.) Default: the role's name in kebab case.

cta.description: The source token for the cta role (The end card's link pill and the start of the avatar's gradient.) Default: the role's name in kebab case.

onCta.description: The source token for the onCta role (Text on the cta colour.) Default: the role's name in kebab case.

captionBackground.description: The source token for the captionBackground role (The caption pill.) Default: the role's name in kebab case.

captionText.description: The source token for the captionText role (Caption words not spoken yet.) Default: the role's name in kebab case.

captionHighlight.description: The source token for the captionHighlight role (The word being spoken.) Default: the role's name in kebab case.

fonts.description: The brand fonts the composition loads.

heading.description: The end card's and the avatar's font; without it, the body font.

family.description: The CSS family name the composition declares and uses, e.g. Inter.

fallback.description: The generic family used while the files load, or alone when there are no files.

files.description: The files of the family: one or more per weight and style, e.g. Fontsource's latin and latin-ext subsets of one weight, each with its unicodeRange. The film picks the file of a character by unicodeRange; OG images try the files in the listed order. None: only the fallback is used.

path.description: The font file (.woff2, .woff, .ttf or .otf), relative to the folder of marketing.json.

weight.description: The weight this file draws (400), or a variable font's range ("100 900").

style.description: Whether this file is the upright or the italic face.

unicodeRange.description: The characters this file covers, as a CSS unicode-range (U+0000-00FF,U+20AC); without it, all of them.

body.description: The captions' and the cards' font; without it, the system's sans-serif.

path.description: The font file (.woff2, .woff, .ttf or .otf), relative to the folder of marketing.json.

weight.description: The weight this file draws (400), or a variable font's range ("100 900").

style.description: Whether this file is the upright or the italic face.

unicodeRange.description: The characters this file covers, as a CSS unicode-range (U+0000-00FF,U+20AC); without it, all of them.

brand.description: The product's name, language, colours, fonts and logo.

baseUrl.description: Where an already running app answers, e.g. http://localhost:3000.

port.description: Port of the app the CLI starts itself when baseUrl does not answer.

startCommand.description: The command that starts the app, as arguments (no shell), run in the folder of marketing.json; {port} is replaced by port.

colorScheme.description: The colour scheme the recording browser prefers.

hideSelectors.description: CSS selectors of elements hidden while recording, e.g. a dev overlay or a floating banner.

screenGuardSelector.description: The element whose text the screen guard reads.

kind.description: What records the film: a phone (touch, framed as a phone) or a desktop browser (mouse, framed as a browser window, 16:9 films only).

viewport.description: The recorded screen in CSS pixels, [width, height]; a phone's at most about 2.6 times as tall as wide, a desktop's at least 1024 wide and not taller than wide.

scale.description: Device pixels per CSS pixel (1-4); a phone needs about 1080 / (640 / width) to stay sharp, a desktop 1.5-2.

mobile.description: Whether a phone's browser behaves as a mobile one (mobile viewport, default true); not allowed on a desktop.

device.description: The recording device (a phone or a desktop browser); a video can override it.

app.description: The app the films and screenshots are recorded from.

provider.description: The text-to-speech service that records the voiceover.

voiceId.description: The provider's id of the voice; part of the voiceover cache key.

model.description: The provider's speech model; part of the voiceover cache key.

language.description: ISO 639 code the voice speaks (en, pl); part of the voiceover cache key.

tempo.description: Speed-up (0.8-1.3) applied at build time, not in the API, so the paid cache stays valid.

minIntervalSeconds.description: Least seconds between two paid recordings (0-3600, default 60; 0 turns it off), counted from the newest file in cacheDir, so separate runs are spaced too.

cacheDir.description: The paid voiceover cache (<key>.mp3 and <key>.json), relative to the folder of marketing.json; commit it.

placeholder.description: The free placeholder voiceover of --placeholder (a quiet tone, words at a fixed pace), to record and render a film before paying for its voiceover.

wordsPerSecond.description: Words per second of the placeholder voiceover (0.5-6, default 2.5); match the real voice to rehearse the film's length.

sentencePauseSeconds.description: Silence after every sentence of the placeholder voiceover but the last (0-3 s, default 0.5).

voice.description: The voiceover: provider, voice, language and the paid cache.

id.description: The film's id: its folder under output.dir and the name social.posts refer to.

title.description: The film's title: the heading of its posts.md and the composition's <title>.

path.description: The recorded page of the app, e.g. /calculator.

format.description: The film's aspect ratio: 9:16 (full screen), 1:1 or 16:9 (a framed phone next to the copy, or a browser window with a desktop device).

device.description: The recording device for this film; without it, app.device.

kind.description: What records the film: a phone (touch, framed as a phone) or a desktop browser (mouse, framed as a browser window, 16:9 films only).

viewport.description: The recorded screen in CSS pixels, [width, height]; a phone's at most about 2.6 times as tall as wide, a desktop's at least 1024 wide and not taller than wide.

scale.description: Device pixels per CSS pixel (1-4); a phone needs about 1080 / (640 / width) to stay sharp, a desktop 1.5-2.

mobile.description: Whether a phone's browser behaves as a mobile one (mobile viewport, default true); not allowed on a desktop.

voice.description: Voice settings for this film only; each key falls back to voice.

voiceId.description: This film's voice; without it, voice.voiceId.

model.description: This film's speech model; without it, voice.model.

tempo.description: This film's speed-up (0.8-1.3); without it, voice.tempo.

name.description: The persona's name on the persona card.

age.description: The persona's age on the persona card.

tagline.description: One line about the persona under the name.

persona.description: The person the film is about, on the persona card from the start of the scene until the persona-out cue or the end card.

id.description: The sentence's id, unique within the film.

text.description: What the voiceover says; also the captions.

pad.description: Seconds held after the voiceover ends the sentence (0-5, default 0.35); only with actions.

actions.description: What happens on screen during the sentence, in order; required on every sentence after the first when the film has no sceneModule.

do.description: Camera on the whole phone screen.

whoosh.description: Play the whoosh sound with the move (default false).

do.description: Scrolls the element into view if needed and taps its centre.

Waits until the voiceover says a word of the current sentence.

word.description: A word of this sentence, punctuation ignored.

do.description: Runs the screen guard now: the video's screenGuard phrases and the current sentence's must be on screen.

screenGuard.description: Phrases this sentence says that the screen must show while it is spoken: checked at a checkScreen inside the sentence, or when the sentence ends. Not on the first sentence.

beats.description: Voiceover sentences in order (at least three): the first plays over the opening frame, the scene records the rest, the last ends with the end card.

still.description: The name of the still action whose frame opens the film.

mark.description: The name of the mark action whose rectangle this shot frames.

word.description: The word of the first sentence on which this shot starts; required on every shot after the first, which starts with the film.

shots.description: Camera moves over the opening frame, at least one.

transition.description: How the opening frame hands over to the scene: fade (a 0.8 s cross-fade), rewind (0.8 s back through the scene in five dissolving frames) or cut.

hook.description: The opening: the result frame the first sentence plays over.

today.description: The day the app is recorded as of (YYYY-MM-DD): pin it once the voiceover is paid for, so the numbers it says still match the screen in a later month. --today overrides it; without either, the day of the run.

screenGuard.description: Phrases the voiceover says that the screen must show at every checkScreen; a missing one stops the recording. May be left out when the sentences carry their own screenGuard.

url.description: The address shown in the end card's link pill, as written (e.g. example.com).

note.description: A small line under the link; empty: none.

endCard.description: The closing card shown during the last sentence.

sceneModule.description: A TS module exporting scene(director), relative to the folder of marketing.json: what happens on screen, instead of beat actions.

social.description: Post copy for the films: the link, the platforms and their channel codes.

linkTemplate.description: The absolute link every post carries, with {code} where the platform's channel code goes.

code.description: The channel code the platform's link carries, so a visit from the film is counted (e.g. ig-01).

linkInBio.description: Whether the caption points to the link in the bio instead of carrying it; default true for instagram, tiktok, youtube.

additionalProperties.description: The platform's channel code and link placement.

platforms.description: The platforms posts go to, at least one: instagram, facebook, tiktok, youtube, linkedin, x.

posts.description: Post copy per film; a film without a post gets no posts.md.

video.description: The id of the film in videos this post is for.

disclosure.description: Whether social.disclosure follows this post's caption (default true).

codes.description: Channel codes for this film only, per platform; each falls back to platforms.<platform>.code.

additionalProperties.description: The platform's channel code for this film.

disclosure.description: A paragraph after every post's caption, e.g. that the persona is an example and the voice is AI-generated; {persona} becomes the film's persona name. A post opts out with disclosure: false.

path.description: The page of the app to capture, e.g. /pricing.

width.description: The browser viewport's width in CSS pixels.

height.description: The browser viewport's height in CSS pixels.

full.description: Capture the whole page, scrolled first so lazy images load, instead of the viewport.

expect.description: A phrase the page must show within 5 s of loading, or the screenshot is refused.

motion.description: The reduced-motion preference of the browser.

minBytes.description: Smaller files are deleted and refused (a blank or broken page); applies to every file of the entry, whatever its scale.

scale.description: Device pixels per CSS pixel (1-4): the PNG is width × scale by height × scale pixels, e.g. 2 for a retina store listing.

colorSchemes.description: Capture each listed scheme into its own <id>-<scheme>.png, e.g. ["light", "dark"]; without it, one <id>.png in app.colorScheme.

scrollTo.description: Capture one viewport frame scrolled to this many CSS pixels from the top (e.g. to check scroll-driven motion, with motion: "no-preference"); refused when the page cannot scroll that far. Not with full.

waitMs.description: Milliseconds to wait after the page loaded (and scrolled) before the phrase gate reads it, for animations to settle (0-60000, default 0).

storageState.description: A Playwright storage state (cookies and localStorage as JSON), relative to the folder of marketing.json, to capture a signed-in screen. It holds a session: keep it out of git.

signedIn.description: Capture signed in through the signIn block: shots signs in once per run and keeps the session in memory. Not with storageState.

steps.description: Done in order after the page loaded, before any gate reads it, e.g. a click that opens a collapsed section; a failing step refuses the shot.

do.description: Replaces the value of an input, e.g. the e-mail of the sign-in form.
